correctness.rationale: The counterexample is exact. For \(X\) standard normal and \(\(q(x)=1-x\)\), q is an admissible decreasing bijection, \(q(X)\) has mean one and so is not distributed as X, while normal order-statistic reflection gives \(q(X_{n-i+1:n})\) distributed as \(1+X_{i:n}\). Shannon entropy and the \(\alpha=2\) density-integral functionals are translation invariant. The general derivative calculation independently identifies the missing additive constant in Lemma 3.1(ii).
